**Time:** about 45 minutes.
**Before you start:** a web browser. The R primers help but are not required.
**When you finish:** you can compute a prevalence, a rate, a risk ratio and an
odds ratio, and say what each one means.

2 short pages. They cover the arithmetic the lectures assume you already have.

::: {.callout-important}
## These 2 pages work without the code cells
Each page downloads about 17 MB to run R in your browser. If that fails, you
lose nothing: every answer is printed in the text as well. You can follow both
pages with a pencil and a calculator.
:::

Do them in order. Primer 7 builds on Primer 6.

## How to work through a primer

1. Open the page. Wait for the cells to become ready.
2. Press **Run** on every cell, from the top down.
3. Do each exercise. Press **Hint** before you press **Solution**.
4. If a cell will not run, read the printed answer and do the sum on paper.

**You should see:** output under each cell, and a green tick when an exercise
is correct.

**If it does not work:** the fixes are the same as for the
[R primers](primers-r.qmd#if-the-cells-never-become-ready). Try a phone
hotspot, or read the page as ordinary text.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why this matters
These 2 pages are mostly reasoning, not code. The R in them is light on
purpose.

Get the denominators right here and the rest of the week is much easier. Nearly
every mistake with a risk ratio or an odds ratio is a mistake about what went
underneath the line.
:::

## Done?

You have finished the primers.
